reference: Documented Git pkt-line/side-band contracts with independently counted fixed frames. One parity case deliberately adapts reference pkt encode using four hexadecimal total-length digits and the input text, then uses GNU private file operations; no GNU pkt CLI exists.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata
pkt encode output and variable assignment for ordinary and empty payloads
pkt decode payloads, length and payload variables, and control packets
flush, delim, and response-end marker encodings
refs parsing for a branch, HEAD, peeled tag filtering, and control markers
sideband channel 1 file output and channel 2 stderr routing
rejection of a declared-length overrun and a short file header
pkt encode frame integration through ordinary GNU-reference private file operations; assigned loadable is invoked.
exclusions: No GNU command implements the pkt builtin interface, so pkt operation cases are honest contract checks rather than GNU parity.
No live Git transport, remote peer, credentials, or real network target is exercised; pkt operations here consume arguments or private relative-path files.
Large maximum-size frames and non-ASCII payloads are outside this bounded deterministic suite.

cases.purpose: Invoke pkt encode (or an independent Bash length-prefix reference adapter) and preserve its frame through relative copy/move/hardlink/symlink/mode/remove operations. The complete tree is compared; this is adapter-based frame integration, not a matching GNU pkt CLI.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t pkt) != builtin ]]; then
  pkt() { [[ $1 == encode && $# == 2 ]]; printf '%04x%s' "$((${#2}+4))" "$2"; }
fi
mkdir pkt-fixture
pkt encode frame > pkt-fixture/body
cp pkt-fixture/body pkt-fixture/copied
ln pkt-fixture/body pkt-fixture/hard
mv pkt-fixture/copied pkt-fixture/moved
ln -s body pkt-fixture/current
chmod 640 pkt-fixture/body
rm pkt-fixture/moved
body=$(< pkt-fixture/current)
[[ $body == 0009frame ]] || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$body"

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata identifies pkt as a builtin, as required for a statically registered loadable.
The Bash help entry exposes the documented pkt verbs and their argument forms.
cases.script:
doc=$(help pkt)
[[ $doc == *'Git pkt-line helpers.'* && $doc == *'pkt encode TEXT'* && $doc == *'pkt sideband BODY_FILE -o PACK_FILE'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'pkt help metadata ok\n'

cases.purpose: Four hexadecimal bytes encode the total frame length; empty payloads have length four, and -V binds the encoded frame without printing it.
cases.script:
pkt encode hello
printf '|'
pkt encode ''
printf '|'
pkt encode hi -V frame
printf '%s\n' "$frame"

cases.purpose: Decode returns the framed payload, -L reports the total frame length, -V binds the payload, and the three protocol control lengths carry empty payloads.
cases.script:
pkt decode 0009hello
printf '\n'
pkt decode 000ahello! -L length -V payload
printf '%s:%s\n' "$length" "$payload"
for packet in 0000 0001 0002; do
  pkt decode "$packet" -L length -V payload
  printf '%s:%s\n' "$length" "$payload"
done

cases.purpose: The protocol assigns 0000 to flush, 0001 to delimiter, and 0002 to response-end; these verbs emit those four-byte markers.
cases.script:
pkt flush
printf '|'
pkt delim
printf '|'
pkt response-end
printf '\n'

cases.purpose: Parse an independently framed advertisement: retain a branch and HEAD, ignore a peeled tag, and skip flush/delim/response-end control packets.
cases.script:
oid=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
printf '003d%s refs/heads/main
00000032%s HEAD
0001003d%s refs/tags/v1^{}
0002' "$oid" "$oid" "$oid" > refs.in
pkt refs refs.in

cases.purpose: A channel 1 packet is written to the pack file while channel 2 progress text is written to stderr; the fixed frame lengths are computed from the payload bytes.
cases.script:
printf '000b\001hello\n000e\002progress\n0000' > sideband.in
pkt sideband sideband.in -o pack.out
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
assert Path('pack.out').read_bytes() == b'hello\n'
print('hello')
PY

cases.purpose: A declared pkt length larger than the available decode input and a short sideband header both fail with status 1 and diagnostics.
cases.script:
if pkt decode 000fshort; then decode_status=0; else decode_status=$?; fi
printf '00' > short.in
if pkt sideband short.in -o short.out; then sideband_status=0; else sideband_status=$?; fi
printf 'decode=%s\nsideband=%s\n' "$decode_status" "$sideband_status"

cases.purpose: A documented channel 3 fatal record returns failure and reports its payload on stderr without pack bytes.
cases.script:
printf '0009\003oops0000' > input
if pkt sideband input -o pack; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ -f pack && ! -s pack ]]
exit "$rc"
